memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "a man found him wandering around in the fields and asked him, 'What are you looking for?' He replied, 'I'm looking for my brothers. Can you tell me where they are grazing their flocks?' 'They have moved on from here,' the man answered. 'I heard them say, "Let's go to Dothan."' So Joseph went after his brothers and found them near Dothan." - Gen 37:15-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
When Joseph arrives where his brothers were supposed to be, they are gone. He wanders in the fields until a stranger notices him and asks, "What are you looking for?" Joseph's answer is simple and, in hindsight, deeply moving: "I'm looking for my brothers." Rather than turning back, Joseph presses on and travels further, to Dothan, until at last he finds them.

Notice Joseph's determination. He could easily have given up and gone home when his brothers were not where expected. Instead he keeps searching. And that persistence, though it led him into suffering, was part of God's larger plan. Even the helpful stranger in the field — appearing at just the right moment to point the way — was part of God quietly directing Joseph's steps.

There is a tender picture here that points to Christ. A beloved son, saying, "I'm looking for my brothers," seeking them out even though they did not want him. So too Jesus came seeking His own, "to seek and to save the lost" (Luke 19:10), pursuing us even when we had turned away.

God, too, seeks us persistently, and He directs the steps of His people through "chance" encounters and open doors we barely notice. Trust His guiding hand. As you go where He leads, He is arranging the details of your path more carefully than you know.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I keep going in obedience even when the way is unclear?
2. How does it move me that Christ came "looking for" us?
3. Where might God be guiding my steps through small, unnoticed things?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You seek us persistently and guide our steps in ways we barely notice. Give me perseverance to follow where You lead, trusting Your hand on my path. Amen.
